evidence: tests/test_manifest.py and tests/test_apply_verify.py provide CPU-only validation of the overlay delivery contract (MANIFEST.json parsing, set filtering, md5 verification).

tests/test_nvfp4_writer_identity.py and tests/test_nvfp4_writer_opcheck.py exercise the production nvfp4_ds_mla writer for byte-identity, CUDA-graph replay, torch op registration, and opcheck schema validation.
tests/test_dcp_topk_pack_identity.py proves the DCP top-k pack is byte-identical to the stock Triton kernel across world sizes, interleave sizes, and -1 padding rows.

campaign-2026-08/sircl/upstream/integrations/vllm/ contains multiple source-contract and fail-closed tests for the Spark TP4 native backends (install, dispatch, port namespace, query contract, graph status, numerical audit).

The blind packet scan evidence flags the largest overlay critical paths as untested: overlays/vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py (3510 LOC), overlays/vllm/engine/arg_utils.py (2866 LOC), overlays/vllm/config/vllm.py (2524 LOC), overlays/vllm/distributed/parallel_state.py (2402 LOC), overlays/vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py (2805 LOC), overlays/vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py (1547 LOC), and overlays/vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py (1292 LOC).

Production overlay paths are validated primarily through fleet benchmarks and probes (benchmarks/correctness_probe.py, benchmarks/midctx_probe.py, benchmarks/sharedprefix_probe.py) rather than in-repo unit or integration tests.
tests/test_probe_dcp4_collectives.py injects a fake torch module into sys.modules so the probe can be imported without a GPU, creating tight coupling to the module's import dependencies.
No snapshot-based tests were observed; the few existing tests use explicit assertions.
CUDA-dependent tests (nvfp4 writer, DCP pack) are not discoverable/runnable via a normal pytest invocation; README instructs running them inside a Docker container with GPU mounts.

test_strategy.dimension_character: The repository has a clear, high-value test core for the overlay delivery contract and the two most critical custom kernels (nvfp4 writer and DCP pack), plus strong source-contract tests for the Spark TP4 native integration. However, the largest production overlay modules—scheduler, config parsing, parallel state, MLA attention, sparse indexer—have no automated in-repo tests and rely on whole-fleet probes for validation, which makes regression detection expensive and slow.
test_strategy.score_rationale: A score of 60.0 reflects a codebase whose tests protect the right things when they exist, but leave the highest-blast-radius production overlays uncovered by automated tests. The reliance on fleet probes rather than in-repo integration tests, and the non-runnable-by-default CUDA tests, prevent the strategy from feeling trustworthy for day-to-day development.

issues.summary: Largest production overlay modules have zero automated tests
evidence: scan evidence marks each of these as 'Untested critical module ... high blast radius' with thousands of lines and zero importers in test context.
None of the root tests/ directory files import or exercise scheduler, arg_utils, config/vllm, parallel_state, mla_attention, sparse_attn_indexer, or the mla/indexer backend.
issues.suggestion: Add targeted CPU-runnable integration tests for the most critical pure logic seams: depth-ladder parsing, scheduler batch-shape decisions, parallel-state one-GPU-per-node short-circuit, sparse indexer width/merge logic, and DCP top-k finish. Use dependency injection or small fixture data where CUDA is not needed.

issues.summary: Overlay correctness is validated only by whole-fleet benchmarks, not in-repo tests
evidence: README.md and docs describe running fleet probes to gate correctness; benchmarks/ probes are not run as part of a CI/pytest suite.

Only the small helper functions in correctness_probe.py and cache_capacity_probe.py have CPU unit tests; the actual benchmark runner logic and cross-module serving assertions remain untested in isolation.
issues.suggestion: Convert the most important probe assertions (byte-identical output vs. reference config, crash-gated shapes) into in-repo integration tests that can run against a local vLLM model runner or mocked engine, so developers get feedback before deploying to the fleet.

issues.summary: CUDA-required tests are not discoverable/runnable via normal pytest
evidence: test_nvfp4_writer_identity.py imports from /w via sys.path.insert and assumes a CUDA device without pytest fixtures or skip-if-no-cuda guards.
README.md shows these tests are invoked with a Docker container mounting kernels/ and tests/ into a GPU image, not with pytest from the repo root.
issues.suggestion: Wrap CUDA tests with pytest markers and skip logic (pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available()), and parametrize device-dependent fixtures) so the same pytest command runs all CPU tests and skips GPU tests gracefully on non-GPU hosts.

issues.summary: Some unit tests rely on fragile module-level mocking rather than clean seams
evidence: test_probe_dcp4_collectives.py creates a fake 'torch' module and registers it in sys.modules before importing the probe, so the test breaks if the probe's imports change.
test_probe_vocab_graph_stream_switch.py similarly builds fake torch objects to test dependency seams.
test_apply_verify.py copies apply.sh/verify.sh into a temp directory and reconstructs a MANIFEST.json rather than invoking a stable Python API.
issues.suggestion: Refactor the probed modules to expose pure helper functions that take primitive inputs or injected dependencies, so tests can call them directly without faking entire third-party modules or copying shell scripts.

issues.summary: The fused DCP gather handoff between indexer and attention has no dedicated test
evidence: test_dcp_topk_pack_identity.py covers the pack kernel in isolation but does not exercise the deferred top-k state or the fused [q | candidates] all-gather in mla_attention.py.
The VLLM_FUSED_DCP_GATHER=2 verification path in sparse_attn_indexer.py exists only as runtime printf instrumentation, not as an automated test.
issues.suggestion: Add a test that drives dcp_topk_defer/take/finish and the attention fused-gather branch with mocked or small real collectives, asserting the gathered candidates reproduce the reference two-gather result and that a missing consume raises the pending-state error.

root_causes: The project is organized as source-form overlays mounted over stock vLLM, so many critical paths depend on the full vLLM runtime and GPU topology, making isolated tests harder to write.
Development validation has been fleet-first: the fastest way to prove an overlay works was to run a probe on the real nodes, so in-repo test coverage lagged behind benchmark/probe coverage.
CUDA-dependent kernels were written as standalone scripts with inline asserts rather than as pytest cases, so they remain outside the normal test runner.
possible_false_positives: Archived subproject files flagged as untested (aeon-crossnode-graphs/, quanttrio-tp4-dcp2/) are intentionally outside the active production test scope.
Benchmark runner scripts in benchmarks/ are meant to be run as CLI probes, not as unit tests; their absence from tests/ is not a test-strategy defect for the probes themselves.

add.header: Core overlay delivery contract has CPU tests
add.description: MANIFEST.json parsing, set membership, md5 verification, and apply.sh/verify.sh argument handling are covered by CPU-only tests. This is the right place to invest because a broken manifest or apply script silently corrupts every deployment.

add.header: Production custom kernels have byte-identity tests
add.description: The nvfp4_ds_mla writer and the DCP top-k pack kernel each have a dedicated test proving byte-identical output against a reference implementation, plus CUDA-graph and opcheck validation for the writer. These are the highest-value single-file tests in the repo.

add.header: Spark TP4 native integration has source-contract tests
add.description: campaign-2026-08/sircl/upstream/integrations/vllm/ includes install fail-closed, dispatch admission, port namespace, query contract, graph status, and numerical audit tests. This shows the transport integration was developed with contract tests.

add.header: Largest production overlay modules are untested
add.description: scheduler.py, arg_utils.py, config/vllm.py, parallel_state.py, mla_attention.py, sparse_attn_indexer.py, and mla/indexer.py have no in-repo tests. Their correctness is only checked through whole-fleet benchmarks and probes.

add.header: CUDA tests are not part of the standard pytest workflow
add.description: test_nvfp4_writer_identity.py, test_nvfp4_writer_opcheck.py, and test_dcp_topk_pack_identity.py assume CUDA and are documented to run inside a Docker container. They do not integrate with pytest markers or skip logic, so a non-GPU developer cannot run the test suite cleanly.
